prompt:
Landscape 1536x1024 (3:2), one individual full-frame background illustration for the existing Bible Journey reader. Match the project’s cinematic realistic historical editorial illustration quality, warm ivory/gold/earth colors, tactile period materials, and natural anatomy. Artistic reconstruction only; do not imply archaeological certainty. Keep every critical person, face, hand, animal, weapon, vessel, and hotspot target inside the left 65% of the canvas. Preserve the right 30% of the image (x=70–100%) as quiet, soft, low-detail scene background for the reader overlay; no figure, important prop, or focal event there. Keep the top 12% and bottom 12% noncritical background, with all faces and story objects between y=12–88%. One continuous scene, not a collage, storyboard, map, or repeated figures. No UI, text, lettering, captions, labels, verse numbers, speech bubbles, pins, markers, callouts, borders, controls, logos, or watermark.

Scene: Numbers 22:21–35, one coherent encounter on a narrow vineyard path with a low wall on each side, as described in verses 24–27. Show exactly one Balaam, one donkey, and one angel of the LORD. Balaam is halted beside the donkey; the donkey is turned toward Balaam with its mouth slightly open to suggest the narrated speech, without humanlike facial expression or any written speech. The angel stands ahead on the path with one drawn sword, clearly visible to the viewer; Balaam is in the act of recognizing the angel and bowing. Keep the donkey, Balaam, angel, sword, and enclosing vineyard walls all readable in the left 65%. Use one continuous illustrative composition compressing adjacent moments from the same episode, not separate panels or duplicate actors. The angel’s form and garments are an editorial reconstruction, not a claim about appearance. Do not duplicate Balaam, the donkey, or the angel. The two servants named in Numbers 22:22 are optional minor figures; omit them if they crowd the encounter, and do not add other attendants, princes, weapons, wings, halos, a divine portrait, fantasy glow, a crossroads, distant city, or modern site marker.
notes: Inspected as one coherent episode with visible subjects. Appearance and materials remain artistic reconstruction. Anchors are authored after image review.
